doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Dream band, reading and closing thoughts
title: Perfect pitch, poor reading and who reads well
summary: She has perfect pitch but calls her reading terrible, and names Dick Hyman, Hank Jones, Fred Hersch and John Bunch as great readers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: I was going to ask you a couple of technical questions. Do you have perfect pitch?
O.k. How’s your reading right now.
Awful. It’s been that way for years. I’ve never been a good reader, because nobody had me learn piano. The only reason I can read at all is having taken violin lessons, which I didn’t want to take.
Yes. Who are the good readers that you know on the piano?
Other than yours truly. No, just kidding.
Oh yes, he’s something, isn’t he?
Dick Hyman. I don’t know who else is a good reader. I don’t know. Probably Fred Hersch.
Yes. Geoff Keezer has very good eyes.

Really? I just don’t know these things about them. I just know Dick, because I’ve known Dick for . . . but he’s ridiculous. He would play a piece of music with fly specs on the music and make them sound good.
Oh yeah. There was another studio pianist who was a contemporary of Dick and Hank Jones when they were doing it. I can’t remember his name.
No, that Milt Hinton used to speak of. That was . . . he . . .

Jimmy Jones was very good, too, but this is someone else who did quite a bit of work. I don’t recall. Once again, we’ll think of that later. Those are some interesting points there. Was there anything else you’d like to say?
